Ecbatana-Iran.name: Ecbatana
Ecbatana-Iran.evidence_basis: 40+ ha core Hagmatana mound plus extensive surrounding urban quarters serving as capital of the Median Empire and Achaemenid summer capital and royal treasury (Herodotus I.98; Polybius X.27; Sarraf 1997; Briant 2002).

Susa-Iran.name: Susa
Susa-Iran.evidence_basis: Proto-Elamite ~25 ha growing to 85-100 ha Elamite metropolis (Carter 1980; Potts 2016), severely reduced after Ashurbanipal's 647 BC sack, then expanding as Achaemenid winter capital exceeding 100 ha with Apadana and dense Ville Royale/Artisans quarters (Perrot 2013; Briant 2002).

Balkh-Afghanistan.name: Balkh
Balkh-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Bala Hisar citadel (~120 ha inner enclosure) and vast irrigated Balkhab oasis capital of Bactria rising from Bronze/Yaz Iron Age town to the premier eastern Achaemenid satrapal metropolis (Bernard; Besenval & Marquis 2008; Ball 2019; Briant 2002).

Persepolis-Iran.name: Persepolis
Persepolis-Iran.evidence_basis: Ceremonial and administrative Achaemenid capital founded 518 BC by Darius I; royal terrace plus extensive excavated lower town (Tol-e Ajori, Firuzi, southern artisan quarters) and Persepolis Fortification Archive ration rolls documenting thousands of court and kurtash workers (Schmidt 1953; Briant 2002; Askari Chaverdi & Callieri 2017).

Anshan-Iran.name: Anshan
Anshan-Iran.evidence_basis: Kur River Basin surveys and excavations by Sumner (1985, 1990) & Alden (2005): ~50 ha Banesh city expanding to 130-200 ha walled Kaftari highland capital of Elam (~28k-38k), contracting in Middle/Neo-Elamite before Achaemenid shift to Pasargadae and Persepolis.

Tushpa-Turkey.name: Tushpa
Tushpa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Van Fortress Mound (Kura-Araxes to EIA) elevated by Sarduri I c. 830 BC into royal capital of Urartu with monumental rock citadel, Menua Canal and dense lower town (~26k-34k peak; Tarhan 1994; Konyar 2012), continuing as Achaemenid/Orontid center.

Old Kandahar-Afghanistan.name: Old Kandahar
Old Kandahar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: 50+ ha walled citadel and lower town excavated by British Institute (McNicoll & Ball 1996; Helms 1997), yielding Achaemenid Elamite administrative tablets as satrapal capital of Arachosia.

Shahr-i Sokhta-Iran.name: Shahr-i Sokhta
Shahr-i Sokhta-Iran.evidence_basis: 150 ha Helmand Civilization metropolis with Proto-Elamite tablets, extensive lapis lazuli craft quarters and a 25 ha cemetery (Tosi 1983; Salvatori & Vidale 1997; Piperno & Salvatori 2007; Petrie et al. 2026), abandoned c. 1800 BC following Helmand delta desiccation.

Rayy-Iran.name: Rayy
Rayy-Iran.evidence_basis: Major northern Iranian Plateau urban oasis (Cheshmeh Ali to Iron Age/Achaemenid Raga of the Behistun inscription and Avesta; Schmidt 1935; Fazeli Nashli; Briant 2002), anchoring eastern Media.

Herat-Afghanistan.name: Herat
Herat-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Hari Rud irrigated oasis metropolis and ancient citadel (Kuhandiz) serving as Achaemenid satrapal capital of Aria/Haraiva (Behistun inscription; Franke DAFA excavations; Ball 2019).

Konar Sandal-Iran.name: Konar Sandal
Konar Sandal-Iran.evidence_basis: 100+ ha Halil Rud Bronze Age urban network centered on Konar Sandal South fortified citadel (~13.5 ha core), monumental North platform and Hajjiabad-Varamin workshops (Madjidzadeh & Pittman 2008; Eskandari et al. 2021; Petrie et al. 2026), contracting sharply after c. 2000 BC.

Dahan-i Ghulaman-Iran.name: Dahan-i Ghulaman
Dahan-i Ghulaman-Iran.evidence_basis: Planned Achaemenid satrapal capital of Drangiana spanning ~1.5 x 0.8 km (~100 ha dispersed monumental blocks, courtyards, fire sanctuary and artisan quarters; Scerrato 1966; Genito 2012; Sajjadi).

Argishtikhinili-Armenia.name: Argishtikhinili
Argishtikhinili-Armenia.evidence_basis: Twin-citadel Urartian administrative metropolis (~50+ ha spread along canals of the Ararat Plain) founded 776 BC by Argishti I (Martirosyan 1972; Smith 1999), continuing as Orontid Armenian capital Armavir.

Mtskheta-Georgia.name: Mtskheta
Mtskheta-Georgia.evidence_basis: Principal urban core of eastern Georgia (Iberia) at the Kura-Aragvi confluence evidenced by the massive Samtavro Bronze-Iron necropolis, Armazis-tsikhe fortifications and Achaemenid-period seals (Abramishvili 2003; Apakidze).

Bastam-Iran.name: Bastam
Bastam-Iran.evidence_basis: Bronze Age mound expanded by Urartian king Rusa II (c. 685-645 BC) into an ~80 ha fortress and planned lower town (Kleiss 1979, 1988; Zimansky 1985), violently destroyed c. 600 BC with minimal Median/Achaemenid reuse.

Kunduz-Afghanistan.name: Kunduz
Kunduz-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Eastern Bactrian fortified oasis city at Bala Hisar Kunduz identified with ancient Drapsaka on the northern Hindu Kush route (Gardin 1998; Ball 2019; Arrian III.29).

Teishebaini-Armenia.name: Teishebaini
Teishebaini-Armenia.evidence_basis: Massive Urartian provincial capital founded by Rusa II (4 ha storehouse-citadel + 40 ha orthogonal outer city = 44.5 ha total; Piotrovskii 1959, 1970), destroyed by fire and abandoned c. 590 BC.

Pasargadae-Iran.name: Pasargadae
Pasargadae-Iran.evidence_basis: First Achaemenid imperial capital founded c. 546 BC by Cyrus II over ~160 ha of low-density royal paradise gardens, palaces, Toll-e Takht citadel and garrison-artisan quarters (Stronach 1978; Boucharlat 2002; Briant 2002).

Tus-Iran.name: Tus
Tus-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal urban center of the fertile Kashaf Rud valley (ancient Susia of Arrian's Anabasis III.25) with deep Bronze-Iron Age mounds across the Tus plain (Basafa surveys; Briant 2002).

Qalaichi-Iran.name: Qalaichi
Qalaichi-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified Mannaean royal citadel and surrounding urban plain near Bukan identified via Aramaic stele and glazed-brick palace with Izirtu, capital of Mannaea (Kargar 2004; Hassanzadeh & Mollasalehi 2011), waning after Median annexation.

Chogha Zanbil-Iran.name: Chogha Zanbil
Chogha Zanbil-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled ~100 ha ceremonial city founded c. 1250 BC by Untash-Napirisha with concentric walls and ziggurat but largely unbuilt outer residential tracts (Ghirshman 1966; Potts 2016), declining rapidly after royal abandonment and ended by the 647 BC Assyrian campaign.

Shahdad-Iran.name: Shahdad
Shahdad-Iran.evidence_basis: Dispersed 60-150 ha Lut desert edge metallurgical, chlorite and bead-making oasis center with extensive Takab cemeteries (Hakemi 1997; Salvatori & Vidale; Petrie et al. 2026), shrinking sharply after 1800 BC before modest Achaemenid oasis recovery.

Ayanis-Turkey.name: Ayanis
Ayanis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Dendrochronologically dated 651 BC foundation of Rusa II comprising a 4 ha citadel and ~80 ha outer town surveyed by Stone & Zimansky (2001) and Cilingiroglu (2011), destroyed by earthquake and fire c. 600 BC.

Estakhr-Iran.name: Estakhr
Estakhr-Iran.evidence_basis: Achaemenid civic and urban settlement 5.3 km north of Persepolis terrace on the Pulvar River, absorbing administrative and commercial spillover in the 5th-4th centuries BC prior to its post-Achaemenid expansion (Whitcomb 1979; Callieri 2007).

Gabae-Iran.name: Gabae
Gabae-Iran.evidence_basis: Zayandeh Rud irrigated oasis settlement expanding into the Achaemenid royal treasury and depot town of Gabae on the route linking Persis and Ecbatana (Strabo XV.3.3; Briant 2002).

Kapisa-Afghanistan.name: Kapisa
Kapisa-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified Panjshir-Ghorband confluence town recorded as Kapisakani in Darius I's Behistun inscription (521 BC; Ghirshman 1946; Ball 2019), controlling southern Hindu Kush passes.

Rusahinili-Turkey.name: Rusahinili
Rusahinili-Turkey.evidence_basis: Second Urartian royal capital and palace-citadel founded by Rusa II east of Van with artificial Lake Rusa irrigation and residential quarters (Erzen 1962; Wartke 1990; Belli 2000), violently destroyed c. 590 BC.

Vani-Georgia.name: Vani
Vani-Georgia.evidence_basis: 8.5 ha fortified Colchian political and temple-city in western Georgia with rich aristocratic burials, gold workshops and imported Attic wares from the 8th-4th centuries BC (Lordkipanidze 1995; Kacharava & Kvirkvelia 2008).

Nad-i Ali-Afghanistan.name: Nad-i Ali
Nad-i Ali-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Large fortified mudbrick platform and settlement mound (Surkh Dagh) in Nimroz/Sistan excavated by Ghirshman (1939) and Dales (1977), flourishing in Iron Age and Achaemenid Drangiana.

Qabala-Azerbaijan.name: Qabala
Qabala-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Fortified 25 ha core urban site at Chukhur Gabala emerging in the 5th-4th centuries BC as the capital of Caucasian Albania (Babaev 1990).

Gohar Tepe-Iran.name: Gohar Tepe
Gohar Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: ~50 ha proto-urban Bronze-to-Iron Age center in eastern Mazandaran excavated by Mahfroozi & Piller (2009), peaking in the late 3rd millennium BC as a Caspian coastal metallurgical and craft hub.

Kabul-Afghanistan.name: Kabul
Kabul-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Highland crossroads settlement of ancient Kabura/Ortospana on the Kabul River linking Arachosia, Paropamisadae and Gandhara (Ball 2019; Fussman).

Mundigak-Afghanistan.name: Mundigak
Mundigak-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: 21-32 ha Helmand Civilization proto-urban center with monumental colonnaded palace, temple and defensive walls (Casal 1961; Shaffer 1992; Ball 2019), declining to a modest Iron Age village after c. 1800 BC.

Haft Tappeh-Iran.name: Haft Tappeh
Haft Tappeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Middle Elamite administrative and cultic city of Tepti-Ahar spanning 14 mounds across ~30 ha core built-up footprint with terrace complexes, workshops and Akkadian archives (Negahban 1991; Mofidi-Nasrabadi 2012, 2018).

Altin Dilyar-Afghanistan.name: Altin Dilyar
Altin Dilyar-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fortified circular walled Bactrian oasis town (~15-20 ha) with Yaz II-III and Achaemenid hydraulic and administrative architecture north of Balkh (Sarianidi; Kruglikova; Ball 2019).

Liyan-Iran.name: Liyan
Liyan-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal Elamite and Achaemenid maritime port-of-trade on the Bushehr Peninsula yielding royal Middle Elamite temple inscriptions of Humban-numena and Shilhak-Inshushinak and dense Gulf trade ceramics (Pezard 1914; Potts 2009; Petrie et al. 2026).

Phasis-Georgia.name: Phasis
Phasis-Georgia.evidence_basis: Milesian Greek colonial polis and Black Sea emporium founded c. 600 BC at the mouth of the Rioni (Phasis) River linking Aegean commerce to Colchis (Tsetskhladze 1998; Gamkrelidze 2012).

Kerman-Iran.name: Kerman
Kerman-Iran.evidence_basis: Highland oasis heartland of Achaemenid Carmania sustained by early qanat irrigation and copper/mineral routes connecting Fars to Drangiana (Herodotus I.125; Briant 2002; Saatsaz 2021).

Shahr-i Qumis-Iran.name: Shahr-i Qumis
Shahr-i Qumis-Iran.evidence_basis: Sprawling Iron Age and Achaemenid settlement complex on the Damghan Plain succeeding Tepe Hissar and laying the foundations for Parthian Hecatompylos (Hansman & Stronach 1974).

Farah-Afghanistan.name: Farah
Farah-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Walled oasis town of ancient Phrada on the Farah Rud trade corridor linking Aria and Drangiana (Ball 2019; Isidore of Charax; Arrian).

Tureng Tepe-Iran.name: Tureng Tepe
Tureng Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: 30 ha Gorgan Plain Bronze Age urban center with monumental stepped mudbrick high terrace (Period IIIB-C; Deshayes 1975; Bessenay-Prolonge & Vallet 2019; Petrie et al. 2026), rebounding as a fortified Hyrcanian/Achaemenid center.

Nishapur-Iran.name: Nishapur
Nishapur-Iran.evidence_basis: Turquoise-trade and alluvial-fan settlement cluster of the Nishapur Plain (Tepe Borj and surrounding Iron/Achaemenid mounds; Hiebert & Dyson; Garazhian surveys).

Tappeh Bormi-Iran.name: Tappeh Bormi
Tappeh Bormi-Iran.evidence_basis: 18-25 ha eastern Khuzestan mound in Ram Hormoz plain identified by Amar-Suena inscription as ancient Huhnuri, the strategic 'bolt of Elam' linking Susa to Fars (Nasrabadi 2005; Wright & Carter 2003; Renette 2023).

Chashma-i Shafa-Afghanistan.name: Chashma-i Shafa
Chashma-i Shafa-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Large fortified Bactro-Achaemenid city, monumental stepped fire altar and defensive gorge complex guarding the southern Balkhab approach to Balkh (Besenval & Marquis 2008 DAFA).

Hasanlu-Iran.name: Hasanlu
Hasanlu-Iran.evidence_basis: 12-15 ha fortified citadel and lower town in the Ushnu-Solduz Valley (Dyson 1977; Danti 2013a, 2021; Lindsay 2026), reaching peak wealth in Iron I-II (IVc-IVb) before catastrophic Urartian destruction c. 800 BC.

Dmanisis Gora-Georgia.name: Dmanisis Gora
Dmanisis Gora-Georgia.evidence_basis: Massive Kvemo Kartli LBA-EIA mega-fortress with inner citadel and 56 ha outer cyclopean enclosure showing sustained year-round occupation (Erb-Satullo, Jachvliani et al. 2022, 2025; Lindsay 2026).

Borazjan-Iran.name: Borazjan
Borazjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Coastal plain oasis housing Achaemenid royal residences at Bardak-e Siah and Sang-e Siah (ancient Taoke of Persepolis texts and Greek accounts; Sarfaraz 1971; Yaghmaee; Briant 2002).

Cavustepe-Turkey.name: Cavustepe
Cavustepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: 8-10 ha linear Urartian twin-citadel and administrative center founded by Sarduri II overlooking the Gurpinar plain (Erzen 1978, 1988; Sevin 2012), sacked c. 590 BC.

Uplistsikhe-Georgia.name: Uplistsikhe
Uplistsikhe-Georgia.evidence_basis: ~8 ha rock-hewn sandstone citadel and cave town in Shida Kartli overlooking the Kura corridor, expanding from Late Bronze Age origins into a major pre-Christian Iberian center (Sanikidze 1987).

Zabol-Iran.name: Zabol
Zabol-Iran.evidence_basis: Helmand alluvial basin market and canal-farming center of ancient Drangiana/Zranka documented in Sistan surveys (Fairservis 1961; Sajjadi) alongside Dahan-i Ghulaman.

Nagarahara-Afghanistan.name: Nagarahara
Nagarahara-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Fertile lower Kabul River valley gateway town linking Achaemenid Paropamisadae to Gandhara and the Khyber corridor (Ball 2019).

Dashly-Afghanistan.name: Dashly
Dashly-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex (BMAC) oasis cluster featuring fortified circular ceremonial enclosure and palace at Dashly-3 plus surrounding farmsteads (Sarianidi 1977; Francfort 2009; Ball 2019).

Dioscurias-Georgia.name: Dioscurias
Dioscurias-Georgia.evidence_basis: Milesian Greek trading colony founded in the early 6th century BC on the northeastern Black Sea littoral, serving as a multi-ethnic Caucasian entrepot (Strabo XI.2.16; Tsetskhladze 1998).

Kef Kalesi-Turkey.name: Kef Kalesi
Kef Kalesi-Turkey.evidence_basis: Monumental Urartian royal fortress, pillared hall and lower terrace town built by Rusa II above Adilcevaz on northern Lake Van (Bilgic & Ogun 1965, 1974), abandoned after the fall of Urartu.

Bampur-Iran.name: Bampur
Bampur-Iran.evidence_basis: Major Bronze Age regional center (~20-25 ha mound and debris spread) in the Jazmurian/Bampur Valley (de Cardi 1970; Mutin 2015; Petrie et al. 2026), later serving as an Achaemenid Gedrosian road node.

Ai-Khanoum-Afghanistan.name: Ai-Khanoum
Ai-Khanoum-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Pre-Hellenistic Iron Age and Achaemenid fortified citadel and canal-irrigated plain settlement at the Amu Darya-Kokcha confluence prior to Greco-Bactrian refoundation (Gardin 1998; Lyonnet 2012).

Godin Tepe-Iran.name: Godin Tepe
Godin Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: 20 ha fortified strategic hub in the Kangavar Plain on the Great Khorasan Road (Young 1975; Gopnik & Rothman 2011; Renette 2023), peaking in Godin III Bronze Age and Median Period II columned-hall manor.

Tepe Hissar-Iran.name: Tepe Hissar
Tepe Hissar-Iran.evidence_basis: 12-15 ha core Bronze Age craft and lapis/copper-trading hub along the northern Khorasan corridor (Schmidt 1937; Dyson & Howard 1989; Petrie et al. 2026), abandoned c. 1700 BC after Hissar IIIC.

Horom-Armenia.name: Horom
Horom-Armenia.evidence_basis: Expansive (~35+ ha twin-spur) Shirak Plain fortified complex spanning EBA, LBA/Iron 1, Urartian frontier garrison and Achaemenid occupation (Badaljan, Kohl, Stronach & Tonikjan 1994; Lindsay 2026).

Ghazni-Afghanistan.name: Ghazni
Ghazni-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Upland caravan town along the Arachosian highway between Old Kandahar and Kabul documented in Italian archaeological surveys of the Ghazni plain (Ball 2019).

Yazd-Iran.name: Yazd
Yazd-Iran.evidence_basis: Desert-margin caravan oasis of central Iran (ancient Isatis) expanding during Median and Achaemenid periods through qanat water engineering (Briant 2002; Saatsaz 2021).

Haftavan Tepe-Iran.name: Haftavan Tepe
Haftavan Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: Massive 18 ha stratified mound (550 x 400 m) dominating the Salmas Plain northwest of Lake Urmia (Burney 1970; Edwards 1983; Dan, Cesaretti & Salaris 2023), peaking in MBA VIb and Urartian-era Level III.

Tall-i Zohak-Iran.name: Tall-i Zohak
Tall-i Zohak-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal fortified tell (~15-18 ha including lower skirts) of the eastern Fars Fasa Plain recorded by Stein (1936) and Miroschedji (1972), expanding as an Achaemenid agricultural and administrative center.

Garajamirli-Azerbaijan.name: Garajamirli
Garajamirli-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: ~20 ha Achaemenid imperial administrative center and Persepolitan-style columned-hall palace complex in the Shamkir Kura valley (Knauss, Babaev & Gagoshidze 2010).

Korzut-Turkey.name: Korzut
Korzut-Turkey.evidence_basis: Urartian fortress (3.1 ha basalt citadel) founded by King Minua plus 9-10 ha unfortified lower settlement in the Muradiye plain, with confirmed Orontid/Achaemenid continuity (Burney 1957; Dan 2024).

Ziwiye-Iran.name: Ziwiye
Ziwiye-Iran.evidence_basis: Multi-tiered fortified Mannaean hilltop stronghold and adjacent settlement east of Saqqez (often linked to Assyrian Zibia; Motamedi 1997; Dyson 1963), flourishing 8th-7th centuries BC before declining under Achaemenid centralization.

Oglangala-Azerbaijan.name: Oglangala
Oglangala-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: 10+ ha fortified citadel and urban settlement on the Sharur Plain of Nakhchivan along the Urartian frontier, remodeled with an Achaemenid-period columned building (Ristvet et al. 2012, 2013; Gopnik 2021).

Sabzevar-Iran.name: Sabzevar
Sabzevar-Iran.evidence_basis: Western Khorasan oasis settlement along the Great Khorasan Road evidenced by Bronze Age Tepe Damghani (Vahdati 2010) and Iron/Achaemenid regional mounds.

Sar-e Pol-e Zohab-Iran.name: Sar-e Pol-e Zohab
Sar-e Pol-e Zohab-Iran.evidence_basis: Western Zagros Gates stronghold marked by Lullubi king Annubanini's c. 2000 BC rock relief and Neo-Assyrian/Median/Achaemenid Halman controlling entry to the Great Khorasan Road (Levine 1974; Renette 2023).

Tepe Naderi-Iran.name: Tepe Naderi
Tepe Naderi-Iran.evidence_basis: Large 10+ ha stratified tell anchoring the Upper Atrak Valley in northern Parthia from Namazga/Bronze horizons through Yaz Iron Age and Achaemenid periods (Venco Ricciardi 1980; Biscione).

Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.name: Shamakhi
Shamakhi-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Ancient Shirvan upland town centered at Khynysly with 6th-4th century BC urban strata and burials precursor to Ptolemy's Kemakhiya in Caucasian Albania (Khalilov 1985).

Minab-Iran.name: Minab
Minab-Iran.evidence_basis: Third-millennium coastal port-of-trade near the Strait of Hormuz with Bronze Age cemetery evidence, continuing as Achaemenid Harmozeia visited by Nearchus (Petrie et al. 2026; Potts 2009).

Pichvnari-Georgia.name: Pichvnari
Pichvnari-Georgia.evidence_basis: Dual Colchian coastal settlement and Greek trading enclave near Kobuleti with distinct Colchian and 5th-4th c. BC Greek cemeteries (Vickers & Kakhidze 2004).

Altintepe-Turkey.name: Altintepe
Altintepe-Turkey.evidence_basis: 5 ha volcanic-hill Urartian western provincial stronghold with Haldi temple, storehouses and pillared apadana reused as an Achaemenid satrapal center in the Upper Euphrates plain (Ozguc 1966; Karaosmanoglu 2011).

Tillya Tepe-Afghanistan.name: Tillya Tepe
Tillya Tepe-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Early Iron Age (Yaz I-II) monumental mudbrick fortified citadel and surrounding Sheberghan oasis settlement predating the later Kushan burials (Sarianidi 1989; Ball 2019).

Keshit-Iran.name: Keshit
Keshit-Iran.evidence_basis: Early Bronze Age urban oasis center on the western fringe of the Dasht-e Lut linking Shahdad and Jiroft (Eskandari et al. 2014; Eskandari 2019; Petrie et al. 2026), flourishing c. 2800-1900 BC.

Izeh-Iran.name: Izeh
Izeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Intermontane Bakhtiari plain settlement complex documented by Wright (1979) survey and Neo-Elamite rock reliefs of Hanni of Aiapir at Kul-e Farah and Shikaft-i Salman, peaking in Neo-Elamite and Achaemenid highland transit.

Tepe Chalow-Iran.name: Tepe Chalow
Tepe Chalow-Iran.evidence_basis: Major Greater Khorasan Culture / BMAC Bronze Age settlement and necropolis in the Jajarm plain of North Khorasan (Biscione & Vahdati 2011, 2015), peaking c. 2200-1800 BC.

Bisotun-Iran.name: Bisotun
Bisotun-Iran.evidence_basis: Strategic Zagros road station and fortified sanctuary town below Darius I's Behistun cliff monument on the Great Khorasan Road (Kleiss 1970; Luschey; Alibaigi surveys).

Tepe Ozbaki-Iran.name: Tepe Ozbaki
Tepe Ozbaki-Iran.evidence_basis: 12-15 ha Alborz/Qazvin Plain settlement complex with Proto-Elamite administrative tablets and a fortified Iron III Median citadel (Majidzadeh 2001; Dahl et al. 2013; Petrie et al. 2026).

Zardkhaneh-Iran.name: Zardkhaneh
Zardkhaneh-Iran.evidence_basis: 30 ha LBA-EIA fortified highland complex near Ahar with multi-room stone architecture, agate-working craft zone and kurgan cemetery (Kazempour et al. 2017; Lindsay 2026).

Chogha Mish-Iran.name: Chogha Mish
Chogha Mish-Iran.evidence_basis: Excavated 17-18 ha Protoliterate regional center of eastern Susiana (Delougaz & Kantor 1996; Alizadeh 2008), contracting during Old/Middle Elamite periods when Susa centralized lowland settlement, with modest Achaemenid reoccupation.

Dvin-Armenia.name: Dvin
Dvin-Armenia.evidence_basis: Continuous Kura-Araxes, LBA/Iron 1 fortified settlement and post-Urartian/Achaemenid town on the eastern Ararat Plain (Kushnareva 1977; Lindsay 2026), suffering an 8th c. BC Urartian destruction horizon before recovery.

Tepe Sialk-Iran.name: Tepe Sialk
Tepe Sialk-Iran.evidence_basis: Twin-mound ~15 ha central plateau center with Proto-Elamite tablets and stepped terrace (Period IV; Ghirshman 1938; Shahmirzadi 2006), largely abandoned in mid-3rd millennium before resurgent Iron I-II (Necropolis A & B) floruit.

Khorramabad-Iran.name: Khorramabad
Khorramabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Primary Luristan valley settlement cluster (Tepe Masur and Khorramabad corridor) identified by Renette (2023) with Ur III Kimash on the copper-trade route between Susa and the Iranian Plateau (Hole 2007).

Artashat-Armenia.name: Artashat
Artashat-Armenia.evidence_basis: Pre-Classical Early Iron, Urartian and Achaemenid fortified hill-settlement across the Khor Virap hills prior to Artaxias I's Hellenistic capital (Zardaryan 2018; Lindsay 2026).

Tepe Surkhegan-Iran.name: Tepe Surkhegan
Tepe Surkhegan-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Susiana fortified mound near Shushtar identified with Ur III garrison and staging city Adamdun (Steve 2001; Michalowski 2008; Potts 2010; Renette 2023), ~14-16 ha at peak.

Tepe Musiyan-Iran.name: Tepe Musiyan
Tepe Musiyan-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled 15 ha regional center of the Deh Luran Plain, plausibly ancient Urua in Ur III texts (Michalowski & Wright 2010; Wright & Neely 2010; Renette 2023), declining in Late Elamite times before Achaemenid canal revitalization.

Chogha Gavaneh-Iran.name: Chogha Gavaneh
Chogha Gavaneh-Iran.evidence_basis: 8-10 ha central Zagros regional center in the Islamabad Plain yielding an early second-millennium cuneiform administrative archive (Abdi & Beckman 2007; Renette 2023).

Kaluraz-Iran.name: Kaluraz
Kaluraz-Iran.evidence_basis: Excavated terraced Iron Age fortified settlement and elite center in the Sefid Rud corridor of Gilan linked to the nearby Marlik royal burial complex (Hakemi 1968; Khalatbari 2004).

Kultepe Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.name: Kultepe Nakhchivan
Kultepe Nakhchivan-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: 10 ha fortified Nakhchivanchay type-site (Kultepe II) with stone defensive walls and deep Kura-Araxes and Middle Bronze painted-ware occupation (Abibullayev; Kushnareva 1997; Bahseliyev et al. 2019; Lindsay 2026).

Zendan-i Soleyman-Iran.name: Zendan-i Soleyman
Zendan-i Soleyman-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified Mannaean and Median hilltop sanctuary-settlement surrounding the travertine volcanic cone in Iranian Azerbaijan (Boehmer; Kleiss; Kroll 1994; Lindsay 2026), precursor to Achaemenid/Parthian Ganzak.

Tol-e Nurabad-Iran.name: Tol-e Nurabad
Tol-e Nurabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Largest surviving stratified tell (~9 ha, 23 m high) in the Mamasani corridor linking Susiana and highland Fars with continuous Banesh, Kaftari, Elamite and Achaemenid occupation (Potts, Roustaei, Petrie & Weeks 2009).

Ernis-Turkey.name: Ernis
Ernis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Multi-period Kura-Araxes through Achaemenid settlement complex and the largest Early Iron Age fortress-necropolis on the northeastern shore of Lake Van (Belli & Konyar 2003; Ozfirat 2021).

Tepe Sofalin-Iran.name: Tepe Sofalin
Tepe Sofalin-Iran.evidence_basis: 12-15 ha Tehran/Varamin Plain urban center yielding numerical and early-to-late Proto-Elamite tablets and sealings (Hessari 2011; Dahl et al. 2013; Petrie et al. 2026), abandoned in the mid-3rd millennium BC.

Tepe Fullol-Afghanistan.name: Tepe Fullol
Tepe Fullol-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: Bronze Age settlement in the Baghlan foothills yielding the gold-and-silver Fullol Hoard linking Oxus, Badakhshan lapis and Mesopotamian-Iranian trade routes (Tosi & Wardak 1972; Ball 2019).

Arisman-Iran.name: Arisman
Arisman-Iran.evidence_basis: 12-15 ha Proto-Elamite copper-smelting and litharge-cupellation industrial settlement south of Kashan (Vatandoust, Parzinger & Helwing 2011; Petrie et al. 2026), abandoned by c. 2600 BC.

Tepe Giyan-Iran.name: Tepe Giyan
Tepe Giyan-Iran.evidence_basis: 3.5-4 ha stratified Bronze-Iron Age tell near Nahavand excavated by Contenau & Ghirshman (1935), anchoring the fertile Nahavand Plain between Godin and Khorramabad.

Tsikhiagora-Georgia.name: Tsikhiagora
Tsikhiagora-Georgia.evidence_basis: 3.5 ha stratified hilltop center in Shida Kartli spanning Kura-Araxes through an Achaemenid-influenced palatial/cultic complex (Tskitishvili 2003; Gagoshidze).

Tol-e Spid-Iran.name: Tol-e Spid
Tol-e Spid-Iran.evidence_basis: Major multi-period Mamasani mound (>20 m cultural deposit) yielding an inscribed Middle Elamite brick of Shilhak-Inshushinak and substantial Kaftari through Achaemenid strata (Potts et al. 2009; Petrie et al. 2026).

Tal-e Ghazir-Iran.name: Tal-e Ghazir
Tal-e Ghazir-Iran.evidence_basis: ~10 ha multi-period Ram Hormoz Valley center yielding early Proto-Elamite administrative tablets and Neo-Elamite burials (Caldwell 1968; Dahl et al. 2013; Petrie et al. 2026).

Yanik Tepe-Iran.name: Yanik Tepe
Yanik Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: ~8 ha fortified Kura-Araxes Early Bronze Age circular-house center southwest of Tabriz (Burney 1961; Summers 2013, 2014; Lindsay 2026), reduced in MBA-Iron Age.

Tepe Nush-i Jan-Iran.name: Tepe Nush-i Jan
Tepe Nush-i Jan-Iran.evidence_basis: 4 ha fortified Median hilltop administrative-religious center near Malayer with fire temple, fort, columned hall and surrounding plain village (Stronach & Roaf 2007), abandoned after brief Achaemenid squatter phase.

Uzerlik Tepe-Azerbaijan.name: Uzerlik Tepe
Uzerlik Tepe-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Fortified Middle Bronze Age settlement mound on the Mil Steppe near Aghdam with mudbrick defenses and craft quarters (Kushnareva 1965; Guliyev & Gasimov 2025; Lindsay 2026).

Amlash-Iran.name: Amlash
Amlash-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Gilan Caspian piedmont Iron Age settlement cluster documented by Japanese and Iranian excavations across Hassani Mahaleh and Halimehjan (Sono & Fukai 1968; Haerinck 1988).

Yarim Tepe Gorgan-Iran.name: Yarim Tepe Gorgan
Yarim Tepe Gorgan-Iran.evidence_basis: ~6 ha multi-period eastern Gorgan Plain mound investigated by Crawford (1963) spanning Bronze Age grey-ware levels through Iron Age and Achaemenid Hyrcanian settlement.

Baba Jan-Iran.name: Baba Jan
Baba Jan-Iran.evidence_basis: Twin-mound (~3 ha) central Luristan Bronze/Iron Age settlement with painted-tile manor and fortified citadel excavated by Goff (1968, 1975, 1985), peaking in Iron II-III.

Tepe Yahya-Iran.name: Tepe Yahya
Tepe Yahya-Iran.evidence_basis: 3.5-4 ha stratified Soghun Valley settlement yielding Proto-Elamite tablets (IVC), intercultural-style chlorite workshops (IVB) and Iron/Achaemenid occupational strata (Lamberg-Karlovsky 1970; Potts 2001; Mutin & Lamberg-Karlovsky 2013).

Sos Hoyuk-Turkey.name: Sos Hoyuk
Sos Hoyuk-Turkey.evidence_basis: Stratified fortified mound on the Pasinler/Erzurum plain spanning Kura-Araxes, LBA/EIA Diauehi-era and Achaemenid Iron Age occupations (Sagona 2012; Lindsay 2026).

Mokhrablur-Armenia.name: Mokhrablur
Mokhrablur-Armenia.evidence_basis: ~4 ha fortified Early Bronze Age Kura-Araxes regional center on the Ararat Plain with perimeter wall and monumental cultic platform (Areshian 2005; Lindsay 2026), abandoned c. 2200 BC.

Qaleh Kali-Iran.name: Qaleh Kali
Qaleh Kali-Iran.evidence_basis: Excavated Achaemenid royal pavilion, hypostyle hall and surrounding road-station settlement along the Royal Road between Susa and Persepolis (Potts et al. 2007, 2009).

Tal-i Iblis-Iran.name: Tal-i Iblis
Tal-i Iblis-Iran.evidence_basis: 4-6 ha Bardsir Valley copper-smelting settlement along the southern plateau corridor (Caldwell 1967; Petrie et al. 2026), peaking in Late Chalcolithic/Proto-Elamite before declining in the 2nd millennium BC.

Shah Tepe-Iran.name: Shah Tepe
Shah Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: 5 ha stratified Gorgan Plain settlement mound excavated by Arne (1945), sharing burnished grey-ware Bronze Age horizons with Tureng Tepe and Tepe Hissar.

Dinkha Tepe-Iran.name: Dinkha Tepe
Dinkha Tepe-Iran.evidence_basis: 2.5-3 ha stratified Ushnu Valley tell with Khabur-related MBA town and Iron I-II occupation (Muscarella 1974; Dan et al. 2021; Lindsay 2026), contracting sharply after Urartian campaigns.

Shortugai-Afghanistan.name: Shortugai
Shortugai-Afghanistan.evidence_basis: 2.5 ha Mature Harappan trading colony and canal-irrigated lapis/tin outpost at the Amu Darya-Kokcha confluence (Francfort 1989; Petrie et al. 2026), abandoned c. 1600 BC.

Tepe Farukhabad-Iran.name: Tepe Farukhabad
Tepe Farukhabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Stratified ~3.5 ha Deh Luran trade and bitumen-processing mound (Wright 1981) showing continuous Uruk-Elamite-Achaemenid village-to-town occupation along the piedmont corridor.
